cumleler: Can your eye act like a tiny battery?
Electronystagmography, or ENG, records eye movement with electrodes on the skin.
With a positive cornea, the eye behaves like a tiny battery.
As the eye turns right, the positive pole nears the right electrode.
So ENG can record even with the eyes closed.
But it cannot record torsional rotation around the eye's own axis.
